newsitem.title: FRANCE: Tunisian prosecutor questions rights activist.
newsitem.headline: Tunisian prosecutor questions rights activist.

text.p: A Tunisian human rights activist has been questioned by a prosecutor about remarks he made at a seminar in Brussels, the Tunisian League for the Defence of Human Rights said on Thursday, calling it harassment.

The league, in a statement received in Paris, said its vice president Salah Zeghidi had been called to testify after his return to Tunis last week from a seminar organised in Brussels by the Friedrich Ebert Foundation. The seminar centred on European Union policies toward northern Africa.
Zeghidi had been detained for a day in October by Tunisian police after criticising his government at a Paris conference.
Police told him before releasing him at that time that he would later be charged with unspecified law violations, Tunisian rights activists said.
There was no immediate comment from the Tunisan embassy in Paris.
In its statement, the league said it considered Zeghidi's questioning to be unjustified as well as an infringement on his freedom of thought and of expression.
"The league hopes for an end to such pressures, which tend to limit his activities both at home and abroad"," it said.
Tunisia has in the past reacted angrily to criticism of its human rights record.
Five international human rights watchdog groups, including Amnesty International, accused Tunisia in September of widespread and worsening rights violations against political opponents.
They said some prominent human rights activists had been prevented from leaving the country while others had been arrested, questioned and threatened with prosecution.
In May, the European Parliament expressed concern over the harassment of political opponents and their families and the absence of press freedom in the North African country.
